== Biography ==
'''Marion Glasgow''' was the sister of [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]], fisher
and burgess of Glasgow. Ninian's 1613 testament left her ten merks and
expressly called her ''his sist[er]''.<ref name="Ninian1613">National Records of
Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/9, images 142–145, testament of
Ninian Glasgow, made 10 January 1613 and confirmed 8 May 1613; working
transcription of the original images supplied 6 September 2026.</ref>

Marion and Robert Fultoun were the parents of [[Fultoun-5|James Fultoun]],
whose Glasgow High Kirk baptism on 7 August 1610 calls him their lawful
son.<ref name="Fultoun1610">Glasgow & West of Scotland Family History Society,
''Glasgow High Kirk Baptisms 1609–1777'', vol. 1/320, 7 August 1610, James
Fultoun, lawful son of Robert Fultoun and Marion Glasgow; witnesses John Howie
and James Barr,
[https://www.gwsfhs.org.uk/records/james-fultoun/ public index].</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Current evidence assessment ===

Marion is Ninian's sister and is confidently identified as a daughter of
[[Glasgow-1096|Robert Glasgow]]. Ninian's burgess admission on 23 October 1596
calls him Robert Glasgow's second son; his 1613 testament expressly calls
Marion his sister.<ref>James R. Anderson, ed., ''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of
Glasgow, 1573–1750'' (Scottish Record Society, 1925),
[https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso43scotuoft/page/24/mode/2up p. 24],
23 October 1596, Ninian Glasgow, second son to Robert Glasgow, fisher,
burgess.</ref><ref name="Ninian1613" /> Together with their shared Glasgow
surname and compatible chronology, these records support the common father.
No evidence identifies a different father for Marion. The existing birth entry is a before-1592 boundary, not evidence that Marion was born in 1592. This is a confident
inference from the combined records, rather than an express father-daughter
statement. Her mother is not identified; the currently attached mother remains
uncertain.

Jonet Meik's 1607 testament also names Marion as a legatee but does not call
her a daughter.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court,
CC9/7/5, images 82–83, testament of Jonet Meik.</ref>

[[Glasgow-3163|Andrew Glasgow of uncertain Corsoun]] named a daughter Marion in his
1597/8 testament.<ref name="Andrew1598">National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh
Commissary Court, CC8/8/32, images 123–124, testament testamentar and inventory
of Andro Glasgw, made 6 February 1597/8 and confirmed 10 July 1598; corrected
working transcription of the original register images.</ref> Shared name and
chronology do not identify this profile as that daughter. No record connects
The Fultoun household to Andrew, Elizat Stevinsoun, Corsoun or Andrew's land,
while Ninian's direct statement that this Marion was his sister establishes a
substantial competing family context. This profile is not the present match;
do not attach Andrew without an identity bridge. [[Glasgow-4095|The testament-named Marion of Corsoun]] has a separate profile while the identity remains unproved.

Marion was named as a legatee in the 1607 testament of Jonet Meik, wife of [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]], but the testament does not describe Marion as their daughter. Ninian's 1613 testament proves their sibling relationship; the currently attached [[Meik-14|Jonet Meik]] mother relationship remains uncertain.

An earlier profile note mentioned [[Glasgow-992|William Glasgow]] and [[Howie-1119|Bessie Howie]]. That association does not identify Marion's father or change the direct 1610 evidence naming James Fultoun as her son and Robert Fultoun as the child's father.

Further research should search Glasgow sasines and testaments for Marion Glasgow or Robert Fultoun naming a maternal relative.

A possible identification concerns Marion Glasgow. The banns/marriage index records Marion Glasgow and John Gray on 30 September 1686 at Carriden.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 664/10 / 109; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected. The combined index date does not by itself identify the precise event type. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Marion Glasgow. The printed Edinburgh marriage register records Marione Glasgow with John Rait, tailor, on 28 June 1659.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 685 / 1/440 / 48; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record]; Henry Paton, ed., Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700 (Scottish Record Society, 1905), printed pp.267 and 560; PDF pp.277 and 570; [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso16scotuoft.pdf#page=570 record]; Same edition, unnumbered Prefatory Note, PDF p.9; [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso16scotuoft.pdf#page=9 record].</ref> The printed transcription and its preface were visually inspected on 30 September 2026; original parish image unchecked. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Marion Glasgow. The printed Edinburgh marriage register records Marion Glasgow with John Bruce, smith, on 4 July 1684.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 685 / 1/440 / 251; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record]; Henry Paton, ed., Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700 (Scottish Record Society, 1905), printed pp.267 and 96; PDF pp.277 and 106; [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso16scotuoft.pdf#page=106 record]; Same edition, unnumbered Prefatory Note, PDF p.9; [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso16scotuoft.pdf#page=9 record].</ref> The printed transcription and its preface were visually inspected on 30 September 2026; original parish image unchecked. The identification remains uncertain.
